entries.exact_value_or_transform: Recorded known limitation with an open door: the v141 server structurally serves one client at a time (listen(4) with accept-and-handle in one loop on both listeners; a second concurrent client is neither rejected nor served but waits in the TCP backlog until the first closes, measured live at 42.1 s LOGIN / 22.1 s GAME with acceptance ~30 ms after release), and the Foundation store closes every open lease of an account inside open_session before inserting the new row. The hypothesis held open by this entry: concurrent multi-client service with per-session state separation is achievable without changing any accepted byte contract, but only after (a) the dispatch thread gains an exception boundary so a stale-lease raise cannot stop the whole server and (b) an explicit lease policy replaces the silent per-account takeover.
entries.scope: Documentation-and-guard entry for the single-session limitation at the accept and lease layers; no src behavior change, no concurrency implementation, no client-observable claim about what a queued client displays
entries.provenance: Project-owner decision on 2026-08-17 (item 14, option B): record single-session as known_limitation rather than by_design, because calling it by-design would assert a client-observable service policy from wire-layer evidence, and open this hypothesis so multiplayer is not foreclosed. Wire measurements are the round-18 job 041 headless probes; the unguarded-dispatch interlock analysis is round 21. GT-003 was released from the attended queue by the same decision.
entries.accepted_ceiling: Recording the limitation and pinning both enforcement layers with tests; the concurrency hypothesis itself has zero accepted evidence and no implementation.
entries.evidence_gap: No runtime evidence of two concurrently served clients exists and none is possible under the current structure. What a queued second client displays is unmeasured. The original deployment's concurrency policy is unknown; no lawful trace shows it.
entries.falsification: Retire the limitation half of this entry if a reproducible run shows two clients served concurrently on the current structure; retire the hypothesis half if a lawful original trace proves the deployment was single-session by policy, or if implementing the preconditions shows an accepted byte contract must change.
entries.stop_rule: Do not implement per-connection threading, selectors, shared world state, or any lease-policy change under this entry. Reopening requires an owner-approved milestone that lands the dispatch exception boundary and the explicit lease policy first, then a two-client runtime experiment with its own ledger review. Stop and record if any precondition work would alter an accepted byte contract.

expiry.decision: Opened 2026-08-17 by project-owner decision (item 14, option B) as a pending hypothesis; it advances only through the owner-approved precondition milestones named in the stop rule.

The session lease is closed cleanly (sessions.closed_at committed, no position rewrite) before any ack byte is queued, and after the acknowledged logout every further frame on that connection is counted and ignored. entries.exact_value_or_transform: Behind the separate ack_close opt-in scenario only (scenarios/logout_hypothesis_ack_close.json, post_ack_action close_socket, close_delay_ms 250), acknowledge the two captured LogoutVital (0x1B40) request forms with the byte-identical hash-pinned HYP-PF-012 echo composition, then perform exactly one additional server-owned action: a clean shutdown(2)+close of that connection's accepted GAME socket, scheduled 250 ms after the ack is queued. No response byte is invented or changed; the ack pins are the unchanged PF-012 values. The session lease (sessions.closed_at) still commits before any ack byte is queued, the dispatch layer is still silent after the ack, and the transport close lever is attached once per accepted connection by the Foundation connection adapter at state-bind time. If the ack_close scenario is active but no transport lever is attached, the whole lane fails closed before the lease is touched: no write, no ack, no partial shape. Wrong payloads, wrong envelopes, wrong sequences, uncaptured subcodes, repository failures, already-closed leases, and every request without the opt-in scenario fail closed exactly as under HYP-PF-012.
entries.scope: Post-ack transport disposition at the runtime-dispatch/connection-adapter boundary behind the ack_close opt-in scenario only; no response-byte change relative to HYP-PF-012, no client-observable exit or character-select-return claim, no default-mode or production request path, no lease-policy or store change, and no effect of any kind under the echo scenario or without a logout scenario
entries.provenance: Opened by the chief session on 2026-08-17 ~20:1x ICT under the project owner's standing pre-approval of 2026-08-17 18:2x ('fix the exit button and every gameplay button found later'), following the GT-007 attended negative (reports/PF_GT007_LOGOUT_ECHO_ACK_CLIENT_TRANSITION_NEGATIVE_20260817.md): the echo-only shape was falsified at the client-observable layer, and the GT-007 GAME_LIVE timeline showed the real client parked on the never-closed socket sending GSCN_RunTimeProtocolReq keepalives every ~2 s with no reconnect and no timeout. The R40 corpus sweep found no 0x1B40 response frame anywhere in the evidence, so no golden logout response exists; the delayed server-initiated clean TCP close is the minimal next falsifiable shape because it is the only lever the server owns that requires inventing no payload bytes. A full GetWorldInfoVital-first shape (0x3D4B before ack) is recorded as the designed fallback and is NOT part of this entry.
entries.accepted_ceiling: Ack with the unchanged PF-012 pinned bytes plus one scheduled clean shutdown+close of the accepted GAME socket 250 ms later, behind the explicit ack_close opt-in only, with fail-closed handling for everything else including an unattached transport lever; whether the real client treats the close as a logout transition is unknown.
entries.evidence_gap: What the real client does when the server closes the socket after the ack is unmeasured: whether subcode 01 closes the game window/process and whether subcode 03 leaves the map (character select, server select, or a disconnect dialog) are exactly the client-observable claims for GT-008 in the attended big round. A disconnect-error dialog would partially falsify this shape and route design to the recorded 0x3D4B-first fallback under a new entry. ATTENDED ANSWER (GT-008, 2026-08-18, both subcodes): the real client never detects the clean server-side socket close at all -- no transition, no error dialog, no disconnect handling for 40+ s, UI responsive; the client-observable exit/transition hope for the ack+close shape is falsified.
